# THE FORGE — FRACTIONAL CFO RECOMMENDATIONS

## REVENUE — CRITICAL PRIORITY

• **Arrest the July collapse immediately.** Revenue crashed 92% month-on-month (£17,711 in June → £1,363 in July); active clients stayed at 151 but AR/M collapsed from £120 to £9. This is a data or cash-collection crisis, not a capacity problem. Check: (1) are July invoices delayed in your accounting system? (2) are members in arrears? (3) did payment processing fail? Until this is verified, all other moves are secondary.

• **Membership pricing is undershooting potential.** June's AR/M (£120) is lowest all-year except July's error. Compare to September–December average (£151.61). With 151 active clients at proper June pricing, you'd hit £18,200+ revenue, not £17,711. Once July data is corrected, stress-test a 10–15% price rise on new joiners (from ~£120 AR/M to £135+); existing members stay locked at current rate. Forecast £19k+ monthly within 2 months.

• **Churn has spiked post-move.** January–April averaged 6.1% attrition; June–July dropped to 0%, suggesting new studio retention is strong. *But* May's 5.74% and April's 8.33% show relocation shook confidence. Lock in the June–July momentum with a 90-day "Welcome to the New Studio" retention campaign: member referral bonus (£25 credit per sign-up), 1:1 onboarding for new joiners, and a studio-feature Instagram blitz (bigger space = new class slots, quieter peak times, more lockers).

• **New revenue line: PT/1:1 coaching.** You have 151 members and zero recorded PT revenue. Even 10 members taking 1× monthly PT at £40–50 per session = £400–500/month. Hire one part-time PT coach on 50% revenue share; train 2–3 staff to offer 15-min "form checks" (upsell to paid sessions). Forecast £500–800/month in Q3.

• **Payroll grew 19% in Q2 (April–June: avg £3,579/mth) vs Q1 (Jan–Mar: avg £3,087/mth), but June revenue was flat (£17,711 vs March £16,259).** You've added staff for the bigger studio—

# Service Menu Build for The Forge

**1. Audit what you're ACTUALLY selling right now**
Before you design menus, spend 2 hours with your top 3 coaches. Get them to list every variation of what members currently buy (unlimited membership + PT, intro packages, class bundles, nutrition add-ons, etc.). You'll find inconsistencies and gaps that kill your margins. This becomes your honest starting point.

**2. Create two separate documents — not one confusing hybrid**
- **Coach menu**: Shows *how* to sell + pricing guardrails (e.g., "Intro PT package: 4 sessions for £X, positioning as onboarding tool"). Coaches need clarity on what's premium vs. entry-level.
- **Member menu**: Shows *what they get* in human language (not "unlimited classes" — "access to all group programming + 1 body scan quarterly + member app"). Prices listed. Zero jargon.

**3. Price anchoring: Start with your most profitable service**
Don't price everything fresh. Identify which membership or PT package makes you the best margin. Price *that* confidently, then work other options around it. If unlimited gym + 2 PT sessions/month is your cash cow, that's your anchor point.

**4. Test and lock in language with coaches first**
Have coaches pitch the menu to 3-5 real members in the next week. Watch where they stumble, improvise, or feel embarrassed. That friction tells you where the wording needs to shift or pricing needs defending.

**5. Lock the menus by [DATE — aim for 2 weeks out]**

# The Forge — Fractional CFO Action Plan

## REVENUE — BIGGEST PRIORITY

• **Rev/member has collapsed to £117–119 (May–June) from £138 (April).** You've grown headcount to 157 (up 41% since Dec), but revenue-per-member is down 15%. Price a tier increase (even £2–5/month on existing members) or audit class capacity—you're running packed peak hours but likely have quiet off-peak slots. A modest £5 uplift across 150 members = +£750/month.

• **Churn spiked to 12.7% in May after the move.** It's back to 3.3%–7.6%, but that May spike cost you ~17 members. Post-relocation, run a win-back campaign on those lapsed members (email + free class offer) within 60 days. Target £400–600 quick revenue recovery.

• **Add a secondary revenue line.** You're not yet capturing personal training, nutrition plans, or PT packages. At 157 members, even 10% uptake of a £40–50/month add-on = +£630/month recurring. Launch in August.

## EXPENSES — COST-TO-REVENUE RATIO IS TIGHT

• **May–June cash outflows (£16.6k–£20.6k) are running 105–131% of revenue (£15.7k–£16.0k).** Excluding the planned April move, your last-3-month average spend is £18.4k vs revenue of £16.9k—a **structural £1.5k monthly shortfall.** Audit staffing (physios, PTs, desk cover): are you overstaffed for current headcount, or is there a monthly cost (insurance, utilities post-move) that's spiked? Share the top 3 expense lines and I'll drill down, but this is unsustainable.

• **July is the bright spot—£8,092 net cash on £19.7k revenue.** You've hit 157 members and cleaned up expense discipline. Hold this ratio: if you can drop outflows back to £17.5k–£18k (vs the May–June £20k), you'll stabilize to +£1.5–2k monthly without further headcount.

• **Target operating margin (before tax & director salary) should be 20–25% on current revenue.** At £16k average monthly revenue, that's £3,200–4,000 operating profit. You're at ~£2k
